subject: [RFC PATCH 1/4] block: do not issue background swap bios as root

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the definition of REQ_SWAP and its relationship to background I/O operations. Suggested that the concept of REQ_SWAP may be flawed, as non-swap paging can also be important for forward progress.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:18:36AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> bio_issue_as_root_blkg() issues every REQ_SWAP bio as root, bypassing
> the cgroup IO controllers, because reclaim cannot stall indefinitely on
> swap writes. Some swap writes are not urgent though: zswap writeback is
> best effort.
> 
> Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> encrypted device").

Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
able to tolerate a failure.

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes to modify the behavior of bio_issue_as_root_blkg() to not issue background swap bios as root, allowing cgroup IO controllers to throttle such I/O operations. The change is motivated by the need to prevent memory deadlocks in certain scenarios, and it does so by introducing a new condition for issuing swap bios as root.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary: Addressed Christoph's concern by clarifying that zswap writebacks are best effort and can tolerate failure, making REQ_BACKGROUND not an issue in this case.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Christoph,

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 11:44 AM Christoph Hellwig <hch@infradead.org> wrote:
>
> >
> On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:18:36AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> > bio_issue_as_root_blkg() issues every REQ_SWAP bio as root, bypassing
> > the cgroup IO controllers, because reclaim cannot stall indefinitely on
> > swap writes. Some swap writes are not urgent though: zswap writeback is
> > best effort.
> >
> > Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> > for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> > deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> > encrypted device").
>
> Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
> and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
> able to tolerate a failure.
>

Yes, I agree, zswap writebacks are only best effort and in case of
failure, the compressed entry still lives. I don't see how
REQ_BACKGROUND could be an issue there?

2026-09-29.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes to modify the behavior of bio_issue_as_root_blkg() to not issue background swap bios as root, allowing cgroup IO controllers to throttle such I/O operations. The change is motivated by the need to prevent memory deadlocks in certain scenarios, specifically when using dm-crypt and dm-thin with limit_swap_bios.

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Pressed Alexandre to clarify the implications of REQ_BACKGROUND on zswap writebacks, and suggested that if such I/O operations can be throttled, they should not be issued as foreground.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 11:16:03AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> > >
> > > Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> > > for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> > > deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> > > encrypted device").
> >
> > Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
> > and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
> > able to tolerate a failure.
> >
> 
> Yes, I agree, zswap writebacks are only best effort and in case of
> failure, the compressed entry still lives. I don't see how
> REQ_BACKGROUND could be an issue there?

The issue is that by definition it doesn't need REQ_SWAP then.

Then again the whole concept of REQ_SWAP looks sketchy to me, non-swap
paging can be just as important for forward progress, so if a driver
needs it, it has other issues anyway.
